Record.title: Marker File Agent Discovery
Record.description:
When a workspace is started, the server shall write an `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` marker file to the workspace root containing the shared host port, all endpoint paths, a machine-readable prompt, and PID. All markers point to the same port; workspace identity is resolved via the `X-Workspace-Path` header. The marker shall be removed when the workspace is stopped.

**Covered by:** `MarkerFileService`, `WorkspaceProcessManager`

Record.title: Memory CRUD tools
Record.description: The QBrain.AI SHALL expose add, list, update, and remove operations for raw-text memories through REST, typed client, MCP stdio, and REPL workflow surfaces.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Add creates a memory and returns ID, text, scope, category, version, and timestamps.
List returns the effective memory set for the active workspace by default.
Update replaces raw text, increments version, and can change scope under validated rules.
Remove soft-deletes a memory by ID.
Invalid IDs, duplicate active IDs, invalid scopes, empty text, and unauthorized scope changes return clear errors.

Record.title: Persist workspace paths with forward slashes and platform tag
Record.description: Operator directive (PLAN-PATHNORM-001, decision D1 2026-10-07: delivered in P1). Persisted workspace paths, storage keys and identity hashes use '/' as the separator for all platforms; the windows: (case-insensitive) / case-sensitive: tag is kept; Windows-origin paths are detected by drive letter (C:/) or UNC (//server/share), not by separator; the UNC leading '//' is preserved; paths are converted to '\' only at OS boundaries that require it (\\?\ long-path prefixes, cmd.exe arguments, native APIs). AC1: C:\Users\kingd, C:/Users/kingd and c:/users/KINGD produce one storage key. AC2: \\srv\share\x and //srv/share/x produce one storage key that still starts with //. AC3: Existing stores are converted by the --workspace-path-rekey maintenance command (decisions D5-D7 2026-10-07): after it runs no Windows-shaped workspace value contains a backslash, per-table and per-workspace row counts are unchanged, and foreign keys validate; the server refuses to start against an unconverted store (no dual-key lookup). AC4: Native file operations on Windows receive backslash paths where the OS requires them.

Record.title: Session turns record current plan file and MCP TODO id
Record.description: Every session-log turn SHALL store planFile and todoId. After persist, query/get SHALL return both fields. They are never null in API output. When no plan or TODO is active, the stored value SHALL be the exact sentinel None (case-sensitive). The first persist of a turn SHALL reject omitted, null, empty, or whitespace planFile or todoId. planFile SHALL accept a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, or a ~/ home-relative path. .. is rejected. Query SHALL support exact filters on planFile and todoId, and text search SHALL match those fields. Existing rows SHALL be backfilled from turn contents and agent history under ~. Import, transcript ingest, and federation apply SHALL persist a validated pair (None if extraction finds nothing). Children: AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-001, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-002, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-003, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-004, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-005, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-006, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-007.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every session-log turn SHALL store planFile and todoId. After persist, query/get SHALL return both fields. They are never null in API output.
When no plan or TODO is active, the stored value SHALL be the exact sentinel None (case-sensitive).

The first ordinary persist of a turn SHALL reject omitted, null, empty, or whitespace planFile or todoId and insert no turn row. A canceled or cancelled supersession may omit the pair, stores the exact sentinel None for each missing value, and a durable reopen preserves that bounded exception.
planFile SHALL accept a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, or a ~/ home-relative path. .. is rejected.
Query SHALL support exact filters on planFile and todoId, and text search SHALL match those fields.
Existing rows SHALL be backfilled from turn contents and agent history under ~. Uncertain results stay None. Invented ids/paths are forbidden.
Import, transcript ingest, and federation apply SHALL persist a validated planFile and todoId (None if extraction finds nothing). Null is never stored.

Record.title: CRUD workspace-scoped use cases
Record.description: The server shall support create, read, update, and soft-delete of workspace-scoped use cases with header fields: title, brief description, precondition, postcondition, scope, and priority. Default queries exclude soft-deleted rows. Multi-tenant isolation via WorkspaceId is required.

Record.title: InstallTestDependencies provisions provider test servers on Linux

acceptanceCriteria.text: On Linux, when MCP_TEST_POSTGRES_CONNECTION or MCP_TEST_SQLSERVER_CONNECTION is not already set, InstallTestDependencies loads it from the test-database env file (default ~/.config/qbrain-test/test-db.env, overridable by the --test-db-env-file parameter) and exports it to the test processes the build starts; a variable already set is adopted unchanged.
It starts the containers qbrain-test-postgres and qbrain-test-sqlserver when they exist but are stopped, and never creates, stops, removes, or reconfigures any other container.

Before tests run it verifies that each endpoint named by a connection string accepts TCP connections, and fails with a clear message (no skip) when the env file, a variable, a container, or an endpoint is missing or unreachable.
Connection-string values never appear in logs, exception messages, or committed files; only variable names, file paths, container names and host:port endpoints are reported.
On Windows, the existing LocalDB and PostgreSQL binaries provisioning is unchanged.
MigrationIntegrationTests on Linux runs the Category=Integration provider tests against those endpoints and fails, never skips, when provisioning fails.

Record.title: MigrationIntegrationTests selects host-specific integration cases by the Platform trait

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a Windows host the target runs Category=Integration cases except those tagged Platform=Linux; on a Linux host it runs them except those tagged Platform=Windows; untagged integration cases run on both.

Every case tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows runs and passes in its own host's MigrationIntegrationTests, so the two lab hosts together execute every integration case, each host at 0 failed and 0 not executed.
The run log names the selection filter (filter text only).
Provisioning is unchanged: TR-MCP-NUKE-018 on Linux, LocalDB and PostgreSQL binaries on Windows.

On a Windows host, MigrationIntegrationTests runs its test processes in an interactive desktop session of the logged-on user, so a Windows case that needs an interactive session (Environment.UserInteractive is true) executes and passes; a run that cannot reach an interactive session fails before any test runs and names the missing session, and never reports such a case as passed, skipped, or not executed.

Record.description: MigrationIntegrationTests runs the Category=Integration cases that belong to the host it runs on: tests tagged Platform=Linux run only on Linux hosts, tests tagged Platform=Windows only on Windows hosts, and untagged integration tests on both. Unit tests contain no platform-specific cases (operator 2026-10-19: "There should be ZERO platform specific UNIT tests.  If it depends on the environment, it's an integration test."). Provisioning stays as TR-MCP-NUKE-018 and the Windows LocalDB and PostgreSQL binaries define it.
Record.notes: IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 plan amendment G, approved by the operator 2026-10-19 ("Yes, I approve the change"). Implementation detail of FR-MCP-BUILD-001; no TEST record. Built tests first in Build.Tests (pure filter function, scripted cases, negative controls), then bound in build/Build.TestDependencies.cs. Build.Tests runs directly with dotnet test as the infrastructure check (operator 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19).

Record.title: Forward-slash storage keys, rekey maintenance command and startup guard

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reuse P1.4 Windows lexical normalization, preserve case, and reject distinct old keys converging before any database mutation.
Apply requires successful verified backup; all database changes and FK validation occur in one transaction; repeat apply is a no-op.
Dry-run inventory and planning run only on a database copy; report mappings, table and workspace counts, and retained manual triage hashes without secrets.
HTTP and STDIO startup refuse legacy Windows workspace ids and point to --workspace-path-rekey.
Recompute only derivable triage, handoff, and federation identities; repoint children; preserve manual triage hashes and rewrite token-store keys with file backup.

Record.description: WorkspaceIdentityPath.NormalizeLexicalPath emits '/' for Windows paths (UNC keeps leading '//'; \\?\ device prefixes stripped to drive or // form); BuildStorageKey becomes windows:C:/USERS/KINGD style. IsRemoteWindowsPath, IsNormalizedPathWithinRoot and NormalizeLocalAdministrativeShareAlias accept both separators. A ToNativePath helper produces backslash paths only for Win32 CreateFile/GetFinalPathNameByHandle, \\?\ long-path prefixes and cmd.exe arguments. Persisted data is rewritten by an explicit maintenance command --workspace-path-rekey (decision D5, 2026-10-07) modelled on McpDatabaseEncryptionTransitionCommand: required backup unless --dry-run, report with old->new mapping and before/after counts; one transaction per database with foreign keys deferred or suspended and fully re-validated (decision D6: SQLite defer_foreign_keys, SQL Server NOCHECK then WITH CHECK CHECK, PostgreSQL DEFERRABLE + SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED); set-based UPDATE per workspace column from a mapping table limited to Windows-shaped values; C# recomputation of hashed values (federation GlobalWorkspaceId/CanonicalWorkspaceId and hub hash-keyed Workspaces rows, TriageGroups GroupKey/GroupId with repointed children, HandoffIngestionRuns ReplayIdentity); FileGitHubWorkspaceTokenStore keys rewritten. No legacy dual-key lookup (decision D7): a startup guard refuses to start while any Windows-shaped workspace id still contains a backslash. Enrolled proxies are re-enrolled once after deploy (only PAYTON-LEGION2 today). Plan: docs/plans/2026-10-07-federation-fixes.md section 4c.
Record.notes: P1.5 operator decisions 2026-10-16: Policy A uses existing Windows lexical normalizer including device-prefix stripping and case preservation. Distinct old keys converging abort before mutation. Manual triage keys are SHA-256(workspacePath|manual|random GUID); retain their GroupKey/GroupId because GUID is not stored. Only recompute derived identities verified from persisted inputs. Worktree-only implementation and disposable fixture/copy tests; no live apply, service operations, deploy, or merge. Current task explicitly requests requirements/tests first (red), then implementation.

Record.title: Required planFile and todoId scalars with None sentinel and backfill
Record.description:
Session-log turn storage, DTOs, REST, MCP tools, and plugin wrappers SHALL expose required string fields planFile and todoId. New interactive creates/submits/beginTurn/replace-turn reject omitted, null, or empty values. Accepted planFile values are a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, a ~/ home-relative path, or the literal sentinel None. Accepted todoId values are a canonical MCP TODO id, ISSUE-N, or None. An EF migration adds both columns, defaults existing rows to None, then a one-time backfill scans turn contents and agent history under ~. Uncertain extractions remain None. Query/get results SHALL return both fields.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001; TEST: TEST-MCP-SESSIONLOG-006

acceptanceCriteria.text: The agent-history scan under ~ (.grok, .claude, .codex, .cursor) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder) and never fails a submit or an import; when nothing usable is found the turn keeps None. Tests that submit imports read the real home, so they are integration tests (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)"; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8).

Record.title: Cross-platform bounded native I/O and deterministic evidence
Record.description:
Use searchable Linux directory modes and descriptor-relative restoration. Isolate potentially blocking physical identity and SQLite pre-handle opens behind finitely owned platform cancellation mechanisms. Classify cancellation from direct operation evidence, and resolve repository fixtures from deterministic assembly metadata rather than mapped caller paths.
Converted from FR-MCP-USECASE-016 on 2026-10-19 (operator: "If it is in a FR, then that FR needs to be converted to a TR"; answers "Merge into its TR (Recommended)" and "FR-001, delete FRs (Recommended)"). FR-MCP-USECASE-016 stated: Use-case persistence and its supporting contained rollback, physical workspace identity, SQLite opening, cancellation classification, and repository evidence paths shall remain safe and finitely completing on every supported platform, including deterministic CI builds, while preserving exact provider failures and truthful supersession evidence.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-USECASE-001; TEST: TEST-MCP-USECASE-019

acceptanceCriteria.text: Linux rollback directories retain owner search and execute permission, nested restoration reproduces file contents and mode, and all mutations remain contained.
Physical workspace identity resolution completes within a finite bound on Windows and non-Windows without caller-thread blocking, cancellation gaps, abandoned workers, or silent platform returns.
SQLite connection opening is finitely bounded before native-handle publication on every supported platform and leaves no worker, handle, callback, interrupt, pool, or lifecycle leak.
Only outcomes precisely attributable to requested cancellation become OperationCanceledException; independent I/O, disposal, and provider failures retain their original type and details.
Repository and Agent Help fixtures discover their root from true external deterministic builds with mapped CallerFilePath and no MCP_REPOSITORY_ROOT override.

Every supported platform executes an applicable native contract assertion in the integration lane: platform-specific tests are Category=Integration tests, tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows when they apply to one host, that run in their host's MigrationIntegrationTests (TR-MCP-NUKE-019) and neither skip nor silently return; no unit test depends on the platform.

The rejected fourteenth receipt is preserved with an explicit supersession notice, and the fifteenth evidence records every failed, inconclusive, and passing run with independently verified hashes and command mappings.

Record.title: Race-safe physical I/O, causal cancellation, and immutable evidence
Record.description:
Resolve and validate physical filesystem identity through interruptible native handles or isolated workers whose public deadlines and accounting remain truthful; bind SQLite opening to the validated object without lexical races; attribute PostgreSQL cancellation to the actual caller cancel request; compose platform-native tests and process containment without pass-through fallbacks; and generate exact-final-HEAD evidence through a mechanically verified immutable workflow.
Converted from FR-MCP-USECASE-017 on 2026-10-19 (operator: "If it is in a FR, then that FR needs to be converted to a TR"; answers "Merge into its TR (Recommended)" and "FR-001, delete FRs (Recommended)"). FR-MCP-USECASE-017 stated: Use-case persistence and its filesystem, provider, process, platform-test, and evidence boundaries shall close physical alias and replacement races, complete publicly within finite contracts, preserve truthful worker and provider causality, execute applicable native contracts, and report only exact immutable evidence while retaining every previously approved control.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-USECASE-001; TEST: TEST-MCP-USECASE-020

acceptanceCriteria.text: Linux preflight classifies each path prefix with statx(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and reads link targets with readlink, so a symbolic link to any path inside a userspace or network mount (not only its root) is rejected from the mount table without sending that mount a request (BUG-BASELINE-009 C1; BugTriage139SixteenthLinuxTests.SqliteOpen_SafeSymlinkBelowFuseRoot_IsRejectedWithoutEnteringTheMount).

The SQLite caller-side data-source preflight runs off the caller's thread under the open's single finite deadline and the caller's cancellation: OpenAsync returns its task at once, a preflight that does not return fails the open with TimeoutException at the bound, no open worker starts, and the preflight stays counted (ActivePreflightCount) until it actually returns (BUG-BASELINE-009 C2; SqliteBoundedOpenFourteenthTests.OpenAsync_PreflightHeldAtBoundary_TimesOutWithoutBlockingTheCaller).

Linux workspace identity resolution resolves symbolic-link prefixes through the mount table before its anchored RESOLVE_NO_XDEV lookup, so an absolute alias within a nested approved mount (for example /tmp) resolves like the data-file and SQLite opens instead of failing with a mount transition (BUG-BASELINE-009 C3; WorkspaceIdentityFourteenthNativeTests.NativeResolver_RepeatedPlatformCallsLeaveNoActiveWorkers).

A bounded traversal or file worker that uses the export root descriptor holds a reference on it from before it starts until it actually exits, so disposing the root at the public deadline defers the close: on Linux the root descriptor stays open while the worker runs and closes after it exits; on Windows the open root still blocks rename (BUG-BASELINE-009, operator decision 2026-10-11 "Fix it now"; BugTriage139EighteenthTraversalTests.EnumerateFilesBoundedAsync_BlockingMetadata_TimesOutWithTruthfulWorkerAccounting).

Physical workspace identity rejects safe lexical paths whose physical target is on an unsafe mount, remains safe across symlink or mount replacement timing, completes publicly within its deadline, and reports any unstoppable worker as active until it actually exits.

SQLite data-source validation and pre-handle opening resist safe-link and check-to-open replacement, use no ineffective Thread.Interrupt dependency for native Linux I/O, finish cleanup within a finite deadline, and preserve exact lifecycle, handle, worker, and exception state.

PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 57014 is translated to caller cancellation only with causal evidence produced by the caller-triggered cancellation mechanism; statement timeout and administrative cancellation remain PostgresException even during concurrent token cancellation.

Platform-specific tests are Category=Integration tests, tagged with the Platform trait of the host they apply to, that run only in that host's MigrationIntegrationTests (TR-MCP-NUKE-019), prove real execution and inventory counts, and never pass through source inspection, skip, silent return, abort, inconclusive outcome, or a below-minimum count; no unit test depends on the platform.

Containment race coverage requires at least one successful contained read and write while proving no escape or corruption, and deterministic total-rejection tests prove that rejecting every attempt cannot satisfy the success gate.

Windows descendant cleanup establishes containment at process creation or proves an equivalent race-free boundary before descendants can escape, and timeout or cancellation terminates immediate descendants finitely without regressing non-Windows process-group cleanup.

Historical rejected receipts remain intact but are explicitly superseded; final evidence identifies the exact immutable tested SHA, contains executable commands or a mechanically complete ledger, independently reconciles hashes, mappings and totals, and limits conclusions to the proven local and retained-evidence boundary.

All current and prior requirements pass focused and cumulative Windows, native Linux/FUSE/non-root, SQLite, LocalDB, fresh PostgreSQL, deterministic external, BDPv4, build, traceability, Release, repository, history, harness, and EOL gates from C:-physical outputs with exact zero failures and zero skips.

Record.title: Marker File Service
Record.description:
`MarkerFileService.WriteMarkerAsync` writes `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` to the workspace root. All markers point to the same shared host port. Uses Handlebars.Net templating with full workspace context. The marker template MUST be loaded from `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` via `PromptTemplateService` (id: `default-marker-prompt`). **CRITICAL**: If the template cannot be loaded (missing file, invalid YAML, or missing ID), the service must log a critical error and shut down the server immediately. Fallback to hardcoded templates is PROHIBITED. The YAML file contains port, `baseUrl`, all endpoint paths, process PID, `startedAt` timestamp, workspace name, per-workspace auth token (`apiKey`), and a machine-readable `prompt` block. Agents should send `X-Workspace-Path` header for workspace targeting.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-018

acceptanceCriteria.text: Agent-plugin version resolution never fails the marker: the scan of the plugin caches under the user profile (.codex/plugins/cache, .claude/plugins/cache, .grok/installed-plugins) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder); a version file (.version or a plugin manifest) that exists but cannot be read (an IO or access error) yields no version, so resolution goes on to the next file and the next candidate; and resolution falls back to the synced plugin version when nothing yields one. Any other error still propagates. Unit tests take every plugin-version input (the agent plugin-root environment variables, the workspace sibling plugin folder and the user profile caches) from test-owned data, never from the process environment, the machine or the real profile, and a full unit run under a hostile environment (every plugin-root variable and HOME pointed at scripted bad data) stays 0 failed (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)", "Fold R3-P3 in first" and "Structural fix, round 4 (Recommended)"; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8).
